official.deadline_note: Applications for the 2027-28 academic session have not opened; the University states they 'will open soon' and invites applicants to provide their details to be contacted when the scholarship is open. No opening date and no closing date are published for this cycle.
official.status_note: The official page announces the scholarship for applicants holding an offer for the 2027/28 academic year and states that applications 'will open soon'; applicants are asked to register their interest in the meantime.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full tuition fee waiver for the duration of study, where you are not eligible to apply for mainstream student finance to cover full tuition fees. Undergraduate students with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding receive the stipend towards study costs only, and Postgraduate Taught Masters students with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding receive the stipend plus a partial tuition fee waiver to cover any shortfall not met by the Postgraduate Masters tuition fee loan.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for the duration of study, where you are not eligible to apply for mainstream student finance to cover full tuition fees
Undergraduate students with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding would receive the £5,000 stipend towards study costs only, if successful

Postgraduate Taught Masters students with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding would receive the £5,000 stipend towards study costs and a partial tuition fee waiver, to cover any shortfall not met by the Postgraduate Masters tuition fee loan
A small number of donor funded scholarships cover the £5,000 stipend only, and by submitting a Sanctuary Scholarship application you will also be considered for the donor funded awards
eligibility: Hold a firm conditional or unconditional offer for full time study at the University of Glasgow for 2027/26 (the surrounding text on the page describes entry in the 2027/28 academic year)
You must currently be located in the United Kingdom and have Home or RUK fee status

Have submitted a claim for asylum in the UK OR are actively appealing a negative decision on claim for asylum in the UK OR have been granted Refugee Status, Humanitarian Protection (HP) or Discretionary Leave (DL) by the Home Office, as a result of an asylum claim

OR have come to the UK through schemes such as: UK Resettlement Scheme (UKRS); Afghan Citizens Resettlement Scheme; Afghan Relocations and Assistance Policy (ARAP); Syrian Vulnerable Persons Resettlement Scheme (VPRS); Ukraine Sponsorship Scheme (Homes for Ukraine); Ukraine Family Scheme
You must have applied to the University before submitting an application for this scholarship
This scholarship is not available to PGdip, PDGE or part time programmes
requirements: You must have applied to the University before submitting an application for this scholarship
Applications CAN NOT be considered without the relevant documentation to support them
Provide your Application Registration Card (ARC) or Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) - front AND back

If you are subject to Home Office Temporary Admission/Immigration Bail Reporting, provide your Immigration Bail Reporting Notice (also referred to as a Temporary Admission Document or BAIL 201) and include every page of this document

If you are not subject to Temporary Admission/Immigration Bail Reporting, provide the most recent documentation you have received from the Home Office in conjunction with your application/appeal, which should show your Home Office reference number
OR provide a share code provided by the UK government that can prove your right to study in the UK
documents: Application Registration Card (ARC) or Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) - front AND back
Immigration Bail Reporting Notice (also referred to as a Temporary Admission Document or BAIL 201) - every page, if subject to Home Office Temporary Admission/Immigration Bail Reporting
Most recent Home Office documentation received in conjunction with your application/appeal, showing your Home Office reference number, if not subject to Temporary Admission/Immigration Bail Reporting
A UK government share code proving your right to study in the UK (available to e-visa holders via the gov.uk view-and-prove service), published as an alternative to Home Office documentation
selection_criteria: Awards are made against the published eligibility conditions: a firm offer for full-time study, current location in the UK with Home or RUK fee status, and a qualifying asylum, refugee-protection, discretionary-leave or named UK resettlement-scheme status
Six scholarships are available; applicants who submit a Sanctuary Scholarship application are also considered automatically for the donor funded awards covering the £5,000 stipend only
No academic threshold, interview, weighting, decision date or notification date is published on the official page
coverage: Full tuition fee waiver for the duration of study, for applicants who are unable to access mainstream funding through Student Awards Agency Scotland (SAAS) or Student Finance
Accommodation costs are not included as part of this scholarship
application_method: Apply to the University of Glasgow first and hold a firm conditional or unconditional offer for full-time study - a scholarship application cannot be submitted before a University application
Confirm you are currently located in the UK with Home or RUK fee status and hold a qualifying asylum, refugee-protection, discretionary-leave or named resettlement-scheme status
Register your interest on the official Sanctuary Scholarships page to be contacted when applications open for the 2027-28 academic session

When the application window opens, submit the scholarship application together with the required documentation supporting your status/right to study, which cannot be substituted with an incomplete set
If unsure whether you are eligible to apply, contact the team using the enquiry form on the scholarships contact page
official.application_route: Apply to the University first, then register interest on the Sanctuary Scholarships page; when the 2027-28 window opens, submit the scholarship application with ARC/BRP, Home Office or e-visa share-code evidence.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must currently be located in the United Kingdom and have Home or RUK fee status, with a qualifying status arising from a UK asylum claim, a Home Office grant of Refugee Status, Humanitarian Protection or Discretionary Leave, or arrival through a named UK resettlement scheme
official.international_eligibility: The page lists eligible countries/regions spanning most of the world, but applicants must be located in the UK with Home or RUK fee status, so overseas-based international fee-paying applicants are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate taught programmes on the published eligible-programmes list; not available to PGdip, PDGE or part time programmes
official.duration: Full tuition fee waiver for the duration of the programme; stipend paid per year
official.description: The University of Glasgow Sanctuary Scholarship supports applicants with Refugee or Asylum Seeker status who are currently living in the UK and hold an offer to study in the 2027/28 academic year. As a University of Sanctuary, the University states that the scholarship provides a full tuition fee waiver along with financial support for living costs. Six scholarships are available to prospective undergraduate and postgraduate taught students.

english_requirement: the scholarship page states no English language requirement of its own

verification.notes: All figures taken from the University's own Sanctuary Scholarships page fetched 2026-10-10 (2027/28 cycle). The page carries two different stipend figures: the introduction and the 'Value' section state £4,000 per year towards study costs (recorded here as the headline award), while the paragraphs covering applicants with funding access and the donor-funded awards state £5,000; both published variants are carried in benefits/coverage. The page also contains a typographical '2027/26' in the offer requirement against surrounding 2027/28 text and an out-of-date eVisa notice referencing BRPs expiring 31 December 2025.

applicant_utility.summary: Six Sanctuary Scholarships are offered for September 2027 entry: a full tuition fee waiver for applicants who cannot access SAAS or Student Finance, plus a £4,000-per-year stipend, with £5,000-per-year variants for applicants who do have funding access. The round is announced but not yet open, so the immediate action is to apply for a full-time undergraduate or taught postgraduate programme and assemble your Home Office or e-visa evidence. Accommodation is explicitly excluded, so rent and living costs in Glasgow must be funded separately. The University also runs a separate Travel Bursary for asylum-seeker students worth up to £50 per month, which is worth pursuing alongside this award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: People already living in the UK on Home or RUK fee status who have claimed asylum, are appealing a refused claim, hold refugee status, humanitarian protection or discretionary leave, or arrived through a named UK resettlement scheme, and who hold a firm offer for full-time study at Glasgow.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply to the University for a full-time undergraduate or taught postgraduate programme first and secure a firm conditional or unconditional offer, because the scholarship application cannot precede it
Before the window opens, get your evidence ready: scan both sides of your ARC/BRP, collect every page of any Immigration Bail Reporting Notice, and download a current e-visa share code from GOV.UK
Check the official eligible-programmes list before committing to a course, because PGdip, PDGE and part-time programmes are excluded
Confirm your fee status is assessed as Home or RUK and that you are physically in the UK, since the award is restricted to applicants currently located in the United Kingdom
Register your interest on the Sanctuary Scholarships page and monitor the scholarships mailbox so you can file in the first days of the 2027-28 window
common_rejection_risks: Applying for the scholarship before holding a University application or offer, which the University states cannot be considered
Incomplete immigration evidence: a BRP image showing one side only, a bail notice missing pages, or an expired share code will sink an otherwise eligible file
Applying to a PGdip, PDGE or part-time programme, all of which are explicitly excluded by the terms
Assuming international fee status qualifies - the award requires current UK location and Home or RUK fee status, so applicants abroad at the time of assessment fall outside it
Losing the award part-way through by failing to report a change in immigration status, which triggers a case-by-case review and possible recalculation of funding
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation, rent and general living costs are explicitly excluded, and no travel support is published, so Glasgow housing and day-to-day living must be self-funded. A separate University Travel Bursary for asylum-seeker students can cover up to £50 per month of commuting costs.
document_audit: ARC/BRP must be supplied front AND back; single-sided uploads are the classic documentation failure here
If you are on Temporary Admission or Immigration Bail reporting, the Immigration Bail Reporting Notice (BAIL 201 / Temporary Admission Document) must include every page, not just the first
The alternative Home Office correspondence must show your Home Office reference number, so check your latest letter carries it before scanning
An e-visa share code is accepted in place of paper documents, but confirm it is live on GOV.UK and covers your full period of permission on the day you apply
alerts: The official page states two different stipend figures for the same award - £4,000 per year in the introduction and 'Value' section, £5,000 in the paragraphs about applicants with funding access and the donor-funded awards; ask the Scholarships Team which applies to your circumstances before you budget
No opening or closing date has been published for 2027-28: the page only says applications 'will open soon', so registering interest is the only reliable way to be timely
If your immigration status changes during your studies you must inform the Scholarships Team, because funding is reviewed case by case and may be recalculated rather than continuing unchanged
One submission also enters you for the donor-funded awards covering the £5,000 stipend only, so a successful outcome may differ from the headline package you applied for

The page's eVisa notice about BRPs expiring on 31 December 2025 is out of date for the 2027/28 cycle - verify your own permission end date directly on GOV.UK rather than relying on the scholarship page
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: University application first and a firm offer, then register interest; when the 2027-28 window opens, submit the scholarship application with uploads of your right-to-study evidence.
